newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris air cargo group to watch truckers' dispute.
newsitem.headline: Paris air cargo group to watch truckers' dispute.

text.p: The air cargo community at Paris Charles de Gaulle (CDG) airport has activated an emergency sub-committee to keep the industry informed of the impact on traffic of road barricades set up by militant French lorry drivers, the Comite Interprofessionel du Fret (CIF) said on Monday.

The CIF, which represents the industry at the airport, said the committee was relaying information to forwarders and airlines on the action by lorry drivers who set up a road block on the A1 motorway near CDG earlier on Monday.
The truckers are demanding wage hikes, shorter working hours and retirement at 55 instead of 60.

One of France's main road haulage operators specialising in trucked airfreight, Road Flight Systems (RFS), said it expected to postpone until Tuesday between five and ten trucking departures from CDG, hoping there would be an improvement overnight.
"Things have got worse as the day has gone on and as we speak a number of our trucks are blocked in traffic en route to Paris," an RFS official said.
Japan Airlines said one of its trucks had arrived at CDG a day later than scheduled.
"Overall, the service is functioning albeit with delays and some of our customers, notably in Spain have become a little reticent about shipping freight through France at the moment."
Air France Cargo said its trucking activities had operated normally over the weekend but the situation could become "critical" if there were a not a speedy settlement to end the dispute.
Swissair said it was maintaining its scheduled trucking service from CDG to Zurich this evening.
The drivers' action, which began on November 18, has now been extended to around 130 road barricades nationwide.
Talks between drivers' union representatives and road haulage bosses, under the auspices of a government mediator, were set to resume at 17.00 (1600 GMT) local time on Monday.
